summary:
The Roots First / Root-and-Branch skeleton holds up: Treasuries back every promise, stocks only back money nobody has been promised, and the 2031 range's bottom is already owned. A fixed-income judge would still find five holes, and all must be fixed before the strategy locks on 6 Nov (IPS-FINAL.txt:73-74).
(1) "High degree of certainty" is never defined in IPS V5. The kit's "never short" evidence uses zero-coupon STRIPS, banned since 6 Oct. On the WInS-listed holdings, about $45k of the $500k depends on reinvesting coupons, and the kit's own historical replay finds a payment short in 65% of start months.
(2) About 72% of that reinvestment risk ($32.6k of $45.2k, MODEL) arrives after the 2033 gift is paid. V5's shortfall order only covers shortfalls "expected in 2033". After that, only Laura's kept half (about $13k at p5) remains, and the kit's chain ends in "her own money", which the case forbids.
(3) Each rung is sized to reinvest its own coupons, the reinvestment-hungry design. A standard dedicated (cash-flow-matched) version of the same ten holdings, assuming waiting cash earns 0%, costs about $309.6k on the 15 Oct curve ($304.1k at 2%). So "certain even if coupons earn nothing" costs only about $5-10k of the 2028 deposit: a simple, distinctive upgrade.
(4) The room under $300k has almost gone: $298,628 on the 15 Oct close, leaving $1,372 (4.7bp). The ladder cost over $300k on 182 of 198 trading days in 2026, with about a 44% chance it is over at year-end. The IBTR note's "about 0.2 points" is now about 0.05.
(5) VT is about 7.8% of Laura's money, with a median gain over Treasuries of only about $4.2k by 2033. The team's own rival memo says All-Treasury gives the facility more at every percentile, and COMPETITION.md:164 and V5:28 state the floor-vs-stocks trade-off backwards for the gift. The branch must be reframed as Laura's flexibility money.
Other gaps: Laura's kept half is promised to three jobs; the 2031 "confidence by construction" can read as a tautology; the floor-size rule can make the branch vanish when yields are low; iBond mechanics are glossed (money-market final months, 0.07% fee, about 60% of money in one sponsor's trusts); each WInS rung pays only about $33-34k while the notes say "$50,000 payment"; the operating reserve's 2033 size depends on 2033 yields ($376k-$439k); facility inflation would leave the $150k floor buying about $118k in 2026 Taiwan building costs; and Taiwan-dollar risk (about ±11-20% over six years) is as big as the whole equity half.

findings.title: High degree of certainty is undefined in V5 and tested only on banned zero-coupon instruments
findings.problem: The case requires teams to define, evaluate and give the assumptions behind 'high degree of certainty'. V5 never defines it and claims each payment 'depends mainly on the US government'. The kit's 'never short' tests use STRIPS (banned since 6 Oct). On the WInS-listed holdings, about $45-53k of the $500k depends on reinvesting coupons at about 5%. The kit's 1962-2011 replay finds a payment short in 65% of start months (single build). The 15 Oct brief's 'no payment missed unless yields fall about 420bp' is wrong on the WInS basis. The team's own WInS notes admit 'reinvested coupons fund the rest', so V5 contradicts them.

findings.fix: Adopt one standard that is literally true for the WInS-listed holdings (for example, covered even if waiting cash earns 0% or 2%; see STRAT-04). Test it on the real holdings, list its assumptions, and delete or label every STRIPS-basis 'never short' figure in team files. The IPS gives the principle; the Final Report gives the tests and figures.

findings.title: Most reinvestment risk arrives after the 2033 gift is paid, and the shortfall order does not cover it
findings.problem: About 72% ($32.6k of $45.2k) of the ladder's reinvestment dependence is earned after 1 Jan 2033. If reinvestment is 2 points below forwards only after 2033, the pooled reserve ends about $10k short (MODEL). V5's shortfall order covers only a shortfall 'expected in 2033'. By then the contribution above the floor has been paid and cannot be clawed back, and Laura's kept half is about $13k at p5. The kit's rule ends in 'she adds her own money', which the case forbids.

MODEL lenses/L03/pooled_1015.txt: 'fwd pre, fwd-2pt post end-2042 surplus $-9,977'
findings.fix: Write into the IPS a rule that covers post-2033 shortfalls without outside money. Options: a buffer measured on the 2033 curve and set aside before the gift; dedicating the ladder from the start; or Laura's half held in Treasuries to 2042 and sized for that job. The 2031 'rounded down' bottom must use the same rule and the same stress.

findings.title: Own-rung ladder maximises reinvestment risk; a dedicated version makes certainty literal for about $5-10k more
findings.problem: V5 reinvests income 'in the holding that paid it', and each rung is sized alone, so certainty depends on 6-15 years of compounding at unknown rates. A standard dedication of the same 10 holdings, assuming waiting cash earns 0%, costs about $309.6k on the 15 Oct curve ($306.9k at 1%, $304.1k at 2%). The own-rung design needs about $327k to be safe at 0%. The extra $5-10k could come from the 2028 deposit before the floor (floor about $140-145k instead of $150k).
evidence: team/google_drive/ips_report/01_version_5.md:26 'with income reinvested in the holding that paid it'
rab/decisions/D_stress_bad_year.md rule 2: 'Each bond's coupons buy a Treasury maturing before the same payment'

MODEL lenses/L03/cf_1015.txt: 'own-rung sizing scaled so each rung pays $50k at 0%: $327,416'
findings.fix: The team chooses between own-rung + explicit buffer, dedication at a stated carry rate (0% or 2%), or keeping the current design and stating certainty depends on coupons earning about 5%. Record the full 43-bond WInS list and re-run the dedication on it. A student rebuilds the LP independently. The IPS principle and the Final Report numbers must follow the choice; the WInS book need not be re-traded, but any gap must be explained.

findings.title: Room under $300k almost gone: the IBTR note's trigger and V5's $292k are stale
findings.problem: On the 15 Oct close the WInS-listed ladder costs $298,628 (room $1,372, 4.7bp; forward basis $2,153, 7.4bp). It cost over $300k on 182 of 198 trading days in 2026, and the chance it is over at year-end is about 44% (MODEL). The IBTR note's 'about 0.2 percentage points' is now about 0.05. V5 quotes 'about $292,000' and COMPETITION.md says 'about $293k on the 6 Oct curve'. The '2027 money buys the payments, 2028 money buys the facility' story is now a coin flip.

findings.title: Laura's kept half is promised to three jobs and is small
findings.problem: The same money is named as the payments' backstop (held in Treasuries 2033-42 under rule 3), the inflation/Taiwan-dollar defence ('equity half') and the cushion for cost overruns or co-sponsor shortfalls. It is about $25k median and about $13k at p5 (MODEL); in the kit's 2008 replay it is $18.4k, against a $30k coupon gap at 2%. The reserve's long bonds (duration about 11) cannot be sold for flexibility without price risk.

findings.title: The growth branch is tiny and the floor-vs-stocks trade-off is stated backwards
findings.problem: VT is about $35k (7.8% of the $450k). Its median 2033 gain over Treasuries is about $4.2k (mean $7.8k, MODEL, JPM 7.0%/16.78%). The team's rival memo says All-Treasury is better for the facility at every percentile. Under the half rule a bigger floor raises the median gift ($175k at a $150k floor vs $152k at $100k), yet COMPETITION.md:164 and V5:28 say the opposite. The 'too timid' criticism is still open, while the case calls Laura 'willing to take thoughtful risks'.

findings.title: WInS rungs pay about $33-34k each but the notes say they fund $50,000 payments
findings.problem: The WInS book is Laura's post-2028 allocation scaled to $300k: iBond rungs are 0.676x and bonds 0.654-0.667x of Laura's rungs. Most notes still say, for example, 'IBTO is for Laura's second $50,000 payment'; only the Nov-2041 note mentions scaling. VT and the floor stand-in were bought 15 months before Laura would buy them. A judge who multiplies shares by about $25 sees about $25k of face value, not $50k.

findings.title: 'Confidence by construction' for the 2031 range can read as a tautology
findings.problem: The gift is defined as floor + half the fund, capped at the top, so it cannot fall outside the range unless the floor fails. The case also asks how favourable and unfavourable markets affect the amount. The range is narrow (typical top about $175k), and the gift lands at or near the top about 3 times in 4. Answering 'about 100%' can look like dodging the probability question.

findings.title: Floor-size rule and the 2027-to-2028 sequence can make the branch vanish

findings.title: iBond ETF mechanics glossed: money-market final months, fees, sponsor concentration, substitution gap
findings.problem: iBonds pay no predetermined amount, and in their final months sit in cash at money-market yields. Weighted average maturities (IBTM 5.71y, IBTR 9.55y as of 14 Oct) imply waits of about 6-7 months before 15 Dec. The 0.07% fee is not in any curve-based ladder cost (roughly $1-1.5k over the life, about today's whole room). About 60% of Laura's money sits in one sponsor's iBond trusts. V5's 'substitute a Treasury maturing earlier' runs into WInS listing no Treasury maturing Feb 2031 to Feb 2036. IBTR is young, but its assets grew from $37.6m to $109.1m.

findings.title: Operating reserve size and composition-over-time not pinned down
findings.problem: Both the case and the IPS brief ask for the reserve's size, initial composition and how it changes. V5 says only that it shrinks. Its 1 Jan 2033 market value depends on 2033 yields (about $376k at 7%, $405k at 5%, $439k at 3%, MODEL) while it pays $500k. Waiting cash (iBond final months; Feb-2037 10.5 months early; May-2038 7.5 months early) and post-2033 coupons have no stated home. SGOV was listed on WInS on 28 Sep, but cash is not on the 14 Oct permitted list.

findings.title: Taiwan-dollar risk is as large as the whole equity half and is not quantified
findings.problem: Over 6-year windows since 1990, the TWD moved against the USD from about -21.7% (p5) to +12.4% (p95), with a maximum gain of +20.2%. A 12.4% TWD rise cuts the TWD value of a $175k gift by about $19k, similar to the equity half's p5-p95 spread ($13k-$46k). Derivatives are banned, so no hedge is possible; the case never names a currency.

findings.title: Overbuilt behind the scenes, under-explained on the page; 'just a bond ladder' risk
findings.problem: The kit has 10 decision memos, about 9 models and 1.6 million paths, mostly on the STRIPS basis. V5 omits items the IPS brief names: liquidity, return assumptions, the certainty definition, and reserve composition over time. The core ladder is textbook liability-driven investing, so without its insights stated, judges may see 'a bond ladder anyone could do'; with model clutter, it repeats last year's over-complexity.

findings.fix: Keep three load-bearing numbers rebuilt on the WInS basis (cost vs deposit, certainty test, where the gift lands). Make the distinctive ideas explicit, each in one sentence: certainty that holds with coupons earning nothing; an owned bottom and capped top so Laura cannot overpromise; stocks only where nothing is promised.
